title: Bellarmino’s two probable views: see all relevant things in God from beatitude’s start, or revelation when we pray
source_text: XLIV. Bellarmino vero ex multis hac de re sententiis duae videntur maxime probabiles. Una eorum qui dicunt Sanctos videre in Deo, a principio suae beatitudinis omnia quae ad ipsos aliquo modo pertinent, & proinde etiam orationes nostras ad se directas. Altera eorum qui putant, Sanctos non videre in Verbo orationes nostras a principio suae beatitudinis, sed solum tunc revelari eis a Deo orationes nostras, quando eas fundimus. Quomodo Prophetae, Deo revelante, cognoverunt futura, & multi Sanctorum hic in terris donum a Deo habuerunt, quo cognoscerent cogitationes hominum, & facta etiam occultissima. Quarum sententiarum prior Bellarmino videtur simpliciter probabilior, posterior vero magis idonea ad convincendos haereticos. De Sanctorum Beatitudine lib. 1. cap. 20.
pass_a_gloss: But to Bellarmine, of the many opinions on this matter, two seem most probable. One is of those who say that the Saints see in God, from the beginning of their beatitude, all things which in any way pertain to them, and therefore also our prayers directed to them. The other is of those who think that the Saints do not see our prayers in the Word from the beginning of their beatitude, but that our prayers are revealed to them by God only then, when we pour them forth. Just as the Prophets, God revealing, knew future things, and many of the Saints here on earth had a gift from God by which they knew the thoughts of men, and even the most hidden deeds. Of which opinions the former seems to Bellarmine simply more probable, but the latter more fit for convincing heretics. On the Beatitude of the Saints, book 1, chapter 20.
pass_b_english: Bellarmino favors two lines: Saints see in God from beatitude’s dawn all that touches them—including our prayers—or God reveals prayers only when we offer them.
He leans to the first as simply likelier; the second as better for answering heretics.

lemmas.gloss: in the Word (God’s essence as known)
